title: Why Pythagoras' theorem works: squares on the sides
examples: How long is the hypotenuse if the sides are 6 and 8?

explain.say: Take a right-angled triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 centimetres. Build a square on the side of 3. Look: 3 rows of 3 makes 9 little squares.

draw.text: Why Pythagoras' theorem works: squares on the sides

explain.say: Now build a square on the side of 4. 4 rows of 4 makes 16 little squares. Can you guess how many fit on the longest side?
The longest side, opposite the right angle, is called the hypotenuse. Its square is 5 rows of 5: 25 little squares.
Now compare the bars. 9 plus 16 is 25! The two smaller squares exactly fill the big one. That is Pythagoras' theorem: a squared plus b squared equals c squared.

Fantastic! It works for every right-angled triangle. Wow: builders still check square corners by measuring 3, 4 and 5 metres. Challenge: the short sides are 6 and 8 centimetres. How long is the hypotenuse?

faq.a: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the longest side equals the two other squares added together: a squared plus b squared equals c squared.
asks: What does a² + b² = c² mean?

faq.a: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle. It is always opposite the right angle.

faq.q: Does Pythagoras work for every triangle?
faq.a: No, only for right-angled triangles. If a squared plus b squared equals c squared, you know the triangle has a right angle.
asks: Can I use Pythagoras on any triangle?

faq.q: How do you find a shorter side?
faq.a: Take away instead of adding. If the hypotenuse is 13 and one side is 5, the other side squared is 169 minus 25, which is 144, so it is 12.
asks: How do I find a missing short side with Pythagoras?

faq.a: It is named after the Greek thinker Pythagoras, but the idea was known earlier. It appears on a Babylonian clay tablet and in the Indian Baudhayana Sulba Sutra, and was also known in ancient China.

facts: The Babylonian tablet Plimpton 322, about 3,800 years old, lists sets of numbers that fit Pythagoras' theorem.

quiz.say: A right-angled triangle has short sides of 6 and 8 centimetres. How long is the hypotenuse?
quiz.why: 36 plus 64 is 100, and the square root of 100 is 10.

wrong.1: 14 adds the sides without squaring them.
wrong.2: 100 is c squared; you still need the square root.

quiz.say: Which side is always the longest in a right-angled triangle?

options.show: The side next to the right angle
options.say: The side next to the right angle

quiz.why: The hypotenuse, opposite the right angle, is always the longest.

wrong.1: The sides next to the right angle are the shorter ones.
wrong.2: The bottom side depends on how the triangle is drawn.
